speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs of the number of children under 12 years old who were injured in taxis and private hire cars respectively in the past five years, how many were not (i) wearing seat belts and (ii) seated in child car seats at the time of the accident.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The latter applies for all motor vehicles except taxis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think we need to understand that the magnitude of problem, and then, decide whether there needs to be a shift in the policy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: From a safety standpoint, why is that an exemption?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know I have asked the Ministry of Transport (MOT) that, but perhaps, I could hear from MHA what their perspectives are.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is not the first time the Member has been asking, and in fact, one is we take his suggestion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And second, since the time he started to ask until today, I think we can agree that there have been positive developments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And if you look back at the answers provided by my colleagues from MOT as well as MHA, you realise that because there are diverse needs within the society, for the transport aspect of it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But at the same time, we also look at the safety of the passengers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And today, you have the ride hail app, which provides that option to those who may want to take this option.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: During some of the pilots that either MOT or MHA had, the response was quite mixed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, I think it is something that we need to navigate carefully, but my personal view is that things have moved positively and we need to continue this journey, putting in mind the diverse needs of our people with safety at the forefront.
